issue.title: average([]) returns NaN instead of 0
issue.problem: math.js exports average(xs), which computes xs.reduce(...)/xs.length. For an empty array this is 0/0, so `node -e 'console.log(require("./math").average([]))'` prints NaN today. test/math.test.js covers add, subtract and multiply but has no test for average at all, so nothing caught this.
issue.reason: mathlib backs the invoice service. A NaN from average([]) was carried into an invoice total last week. NaN spreads silently through any arithmetic it touches.
issue.outcome: average([]) returns 0. average on non-empty arrays still returns the arithmetic mean. The test suite covers both cases, so the bug cannot come back unnoticed.
expect: `node -e 'const r=require("./math").average([]); console.log(Object.is(r,0))'` run from the repo root prints `true` (the result is the number 0, not NaN, -0, null or a string)
`node -e 'const {average}=require("./math"); console.log(average([1,2,3]), average([5]), average([-2,2]), average([1,2]))'` prints `2 5 0 1.5`, so non-empty averages are unchanged
`node -e 'const m=require("./math"); console.log(Object.keys(m).sort().join(","))'` prints `add,average,multiply,subtract`, so the exports are unchanged
`npm test` exits 0, and the suite has a test that calls average([]) and asserts the result is 0
Regression check: with only math.js's average reverted to the current `xs.reduce((sum, x) => sum + x, 0) / xs.length` body (and the PR's tests kept), `npm test` exits non-zero

non_goals: Changing how average handles non-array input, non-numeric elements, or NaN/Infinity inside the list
Changes to the invoice service or to past invoice totals
assumptions: The request says an empty list should average to 0, so this issue uses the number 0 rather than throwing an error or returning null.
Only the empty array is special-cased. Other edge inputs (undefined, non-arrays) are out of scope and may behave as they do today.
A package version bump or README update is optional and not required.
